An early convert to Islam and a commander at the Battle of Badr in 624, this Arab Muslim general fought in the Ridda Wars and the early conquests of Persia, Syria and North Africa — who was he?
Zubayr ibn al-Awwam: Arab Muslim military commander (594–656)
Who among these was born first?
Henry Vaughan (born 1621) is the earliest of the four.
Which of these people was born first?
Ada Lovelace (born 1815) is the earliest of the four.
Which one below was established earliest?
Bash (Unix shell) (founded 1989) is the earliest of the four.
Which of these four appeared earliest?
SQL (published 1986) is the earliest of the four.
Which of these four is a physicist?
Edwin McMillan is a physicist. McMillan co-invented the synchrotron with Vladimir Veksler, and after the war he returned to the Berkeley Radiation Laboratory to build them.
Pick the chemist from these four.
Maud Menten is a chemist. Maud Leonora Menten (March 20, 1879 – July 17, 1960) was a Canadian physician and chemist.
What is the atomic number of Silicon?
Silicon (SILL-ih-kən) is a chemical element; it has symbol Si and atomic number 14.
In what year was Max Born?
Max Born: During World War I, Born was originally placed as a radio operator, but his specialist knowledge led to his being moved to research duties on sound ranging.
In what year was Fermat's Last Theorem discovered?
Fermat's Last Theorem: The proposition was first stated as a theorem by Pierre de Fermat around 1637 in the margin of a copy of Arithmetica.
In what year was Selenium discovered?
Selenium is a chemical element; it has symbol Se and atomic number 34.
Metoprolol: Pfizer. It is also used to prevent further heart problems after myocardial infarction and to prevent headaches in those with migraines.
Publishing: Germany. It has various divisions such as trade/retail publishing of fiction and non-fiction, educational publishing, and academic and scientific publishing.
Who is credited with discovering Malaria?
Malaria: Ronald Ross. Malaria is a mosquito-borne infectious disease that is transmitted by the bite of Anopheles mosquitoes.
Who is credited with discovering Kwashiorkor?
Kwashiorkor: Cicely Williams. Kwashiorkor ( KWOSH-ee-OR-kor, -⁠kər) is a form of severe protein malnutrition characterized by edema and an enlarged liver with fatty infiltrates.
Who is credited with discovering Titanium?
Titanium: William Gregor. Titanium is a chemical element; it has symbol Ti and atomic number 22.
When a message is designed to spark an immediate purchase, it's called the 'direct-response' kind of this consumer-facing practice. What is it?
Advertising is the practice and techniques employed to bring attention to a product or service.
Named after a French physicist considered a father of electromagnetism, this SI unit measures electric current as one coulomb of charge passing a point per second. What unit is it?
Ampere (symbol: A), often shortened to amp, is the unit of electric current in the International System of Units (SI).
More than 500 orb-weaving spider species, including the familiar garden spider, belong to this genus first classified in 1757 — which genus?
Araneus is a genus of common orb-weaving spiders with more than 500 species, among which are the European garden spider and the barn spider.

These shelled marine crustaceans, cousins to crabs and lobsters, spend their adult lives cemented in place filtering food from the water — and folklore once claimed geese hatched fully formed from one variety. What are they?
Barnacle are arthropods of the subclass Cirripedia in the subphylum Crustacea.

Thought to be the world's most abundant bird of prey in its family, with an estimated 6.7 million individuals, this opportunistic raptor is known for its angled wings and distinctive forked tail — what is it?
Black kite (Milvus migrans) is a medium-sized bird of prey in the family Accipitridae, which also includes many other diurnal raptors.

This shield-shaped insect, native to East Asia, was accidentally introduced to Allentown, Pennsylvania in 1998 and became a major agricultural pest feeding on over 100 plant species — what insect is it?
Brown marmorated stink bug (Halyomorpha halys) is an insect in the family Pentatomidae, native to China, Japan, Korea, and other Asian regions.

Once thought to not really exist as a stable molecule, this compound was confirmed since around 1990 to have a real, if fleeting, existence — lasting only about 20 milliseconds at body temperature — what compound is it?
Carbonic acid is a chemical compound with the chemical formula H2CO3.
Atomic number 17, this strongly oxidising yellow-green gas sits between fluorine and bromine on the periodic table — what element is it?
Chlorine is a chemical element; it has symbol Cl and atomic number 17.
What's the scientific family name for the group of birds that includes both doves and pigeons — stout-bodied birds with small heads and no formal distinction between the two common names?
Columbidae is a bird family consisting of doves and pigeons.
Bottle gourds, bitter melon, and the fibrous fruit that gives us loofah sponges are all members of which roughly 965-species plant family?
Cucurbitaceae (kew-), also called cucurbits or the gourd family, are a plant family consisting of about 965 species in 101 genera.
First discovered in 1877 and named the following year for its unique double-beamed tail bones, this genus of long-necked sauropod dinosaur roamed Late Jurassic North America — what is it?
Diplodocus (or) is an extinct genus of diplodocid sauropod dinosaurs known from the Late Jurassic of North America.
This mammal family includes living species from two genera as well as extinct giants like the woolly mammoth, and was first scientifically described in 1821 — what family is it?

Elephantidae is a family of large, herbivorous proboscidean mammals which includes the living elephants (belonging to the genera Elephas and Loxodonta), as well as a number of extinct genera like Mammuthus (mammoths) and Palaeoloxodon.

The telltale earth mounds this tunneling mammal pushes to the surface come from its constantly expanding burrow system, and it feeds mainly on earthworms paralyzed by toxins in its saliva — what animal is it?
European mole (Talpa europaea) is a mammal of the order Eulipotyphla.
This American physician-scientist discovered genes tied to several diseases, led the Human Genome Project, and went on to direct the NIH under three presidents — who is he?
Francis Collins (born April 14, 1950) is an American physician-scientist who discovered the genes associated with a number of diseases and led the Human Genome Project.

A 1946 civilian demonstrator version of this British fighter became the world's first civilian-registered jet aircraft, decades after it debuted as the Allies' sole combat jet of World War II — which aircraft?
Gloster Meteor was the first British jet fighter and the Allies' only jet aircraft to engage in combat operations during the Second World War.

This herbivorous mammal, the largest in its family of lagomorphs, nests in shallow ground depressions called 'forms' and is built for speed with long hind legs and heat-dissipating ears — what animal is it?
Hare are mammals belonging to the genus Lepus.
This American physicist threw out the wave-function collapse postulate, instead folding the observer into the same quantum state — an idea later known as the many-worlds interpretation. Who was he?
Hugh Everett III (November 11, 1930 - July 19, 1982) was an American physicist who proposed the relative state interpretation of quantum mechanics.

According to Alfred Adler, this persistent psychological feeling of being deficient compared to others — often rooted in childhood upbringing or social status — can drive a person to overcompensate. Name the concept?
Inferiority complex is a consistent feeling of inadequacy, often resulting in the belief that one is in some way deficient, or inferior, to others.
A former Chicago financial options trader, this internet entrepreneur co-founded a nonprofit free encyclopedia as well as the for-profit wiki host Fandom — who is he?
Jimmy Wales (born August 8, 1966) is an American and British internet entrepreneur and former financial trader.

Normally part of the healthy flora in the mouth, skin, and gut, this rod-shaped bacterium can turn destructive if aspirated into the lungs, producing a telltale bloody, brick-colored jelly-like sputum — what's the organism?
Klebsiella pneumoniae is a Gram-negative, non-motile, encapsulated, lactose-fermenting, facultative anaerobic, rod-shaped bacterium.

Equal to about 9.46 trillion kilometres, this astronomical distance unit is defined by how far illumination travels through a vacuum in 365.25 days — despite its name, it isn't a measure of time. What is it?
Light-year (ly or lyr), is a unit of length used to express astronomical distances and is equal to exactly 9460730472580.8 km, which is approximately 9.46 trillion kilometres or 5.88 trillion miles.
Which Australian nut-producing tree genus, an important bushfood for Aboriginal peoples, was first commercially cultivated at scale not in its native country but in Hawaii?
Macadamia is a genus of four species of trees in the flowering plant family Proteaceae.
This cone-shaped structure at the base of the brainstem controls involuntary functions from heart rate and breathing to vomiting and sneezing — what is it called?
Medulla oblongata is a long stem-like structure which makes up the lower part of the brainstem.
By dividing one cell into two with an identical set of chromosomes apiece, this stage of the cell cycle keeps genetic stability intact across generations — what is it?
Mitosis is a part of the cell cycle in eukaryotic cells in which replicated chromosomes are separated into two new nuclei.

This chronic neurological disorder scrambles the sleep-wake cycle, attacking REM sleep with daytime drowsiness, sleep paralysis, and cataplexy — sudden episodes where muscle tone simply vanishes. What is it?
Narcolepsy is a chronic neurological disorder that impairs the ability to regulate sleep-wake cycles, and specifically impacts REM (rapid eye movement) sleep.

Classified using a measurement of weight divided by the square of height, this medical condition is diagnosed when that figure exceeds 30 and is linked to cardiovascular disease and type 2 diabetes — what is it?
Obesity is a medical condition, considered a disease by multiple organizations, in which excess body fat has accumulated to such an extent that it can have negative effects on health.
Pair it with aspirin and caffeine and it's a first-line remedy for mild headaches; on its own it's the active ingredient many people know as acetaminophen — what is this over-the-counter drug?
Paracetamol is an analgesic and antipyretic agent used to treat fever and mild to moderate pain.
This inflammation of the back of the throat causes a sore throat and fever, most often from a viral infection, though strep bacteria cause roughly a quarter of cases in children — name the condition?
Pharyngitis is inflammation of the back of the throat, known as the pharynx.
Cough, chest pain, fever, and trouble breathing point to this infection of the lungs' alveoli, often classified by where it was caught — community or hospital — what is it?
Pneumonia is an inflammatory condition of the lung primarily affecting the small air sacs known as alveoli.

This sympathomimetic medication is best known as a nasal decongestant, though at higher doses it can act as a stimulant and appetite suppressant, making it a common drug of abuse — what's the compound called?
Pseudoephedrine is a sympathomimetic medication which is used as a nasal decongestant to treat nasal congestion.
Named from the Latin word for 'net', this light-sensitive layer lining the back of the eye functions much like the film or sensor inside a camera. Name this part of the eye?

This zodiac constellation, whose Latin name means 'archer,' is traditionally depicted as a centaur drawing a bow, and its territory in the southern sky contains the center of the Milky Way galaxy. What constellation is this?
Sagittarius (constellation) is one of the constellations of the zodiac and is located in the Southern celestial hemisphere.

Drawing on tools from anthropology, biology, medicine, psychology, and criminology, this scientific field studies human sexual interests, behaviors, and functions, distinct from purely social commentary on the subject — what is this field called?
Sexology is the scientific study of human sexuality, including human sexual interests, behaviors, and functions.
Beginning with stem cells near the basement membrane and passing through two rounds of meiosis, this process turns germ cells into haploid sperm inside the seminiferous tubules — what is it called?
Spermatogenesis is the process by which haploid spermatozoa develop from germ cells in the seminiferous tubules of the testicle.

Practiced by professionals who determine property boundaries and construction points using total stations, GNSS receivers, and lidar sensors, which technical discipline combines geometry, trigonometry, and law?
Surveying is the technique, profession, art, and science of determining the terrestrial positions of points based on the distances and angles between them.

In 1933 he won the Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine for discoveries about the role of chromosomes in heredity, studying fruit-fly genetics after the rediscovery of Mendelian inheritance in 1900—who was this pioneering biologist?
Thomas Hunt Morgan (September 25, 1866 - December 4, 1945) was an American evolutionary biologist, geneticist, and embryologist.
Built in the Soviet Union from 1966 to 1989 for short-haul routes, this narrow-body jet earned the NATO codename 'Crusty' — which airliner is it?
Tupolev Tu-134 (NATO reporting name: Crusty) is a twin-engined, narrow-body jet airliner built in the Soviet Union for short and medium-haul routes from 1966 to 1989.

Many of these carrion-eating birds sport a bald head that stays clean while feeding and helps with temperature control — and they'll even urinate on their own legs to cool off. What kind of bird is it?
Vulture is a bird of prey that scavenges on carrion.
Atomic number 30, mined mostly from the ore sphalerite, this metal turns shiny blue-white once its surface oxidation is removed — which element?
Zinc is a chemical element; it has symbol Zn and atomic number 30.
Nicknamed the cell's "molecular unit of currency," this energy-carrying molecule powers muscle contraction and nerve impulses, dropping to ADP or AMP when spent — what is it?
Adenosine triphosphate: Energy-carrying molecule in living cells.
Sometimes called 'emotional blindness,' this condition makes it hard to identify or describe one's own feelings, and affects roughly half of people with autism. What is it?
Alexithymia: Deficiency in understanding, processing, or describing emotions.
Nicknamed the corpse flower for its rotting-flesh stench, this Sumatran plant first bloomed in cultivation at Kew Gardens in 1889 — which species?
Amorphophallus titanum: Species of flowering plant in the arum family Araceae.
NATO code-named 'Condor,' this Soviet-designed four-engine giant is the largest military transport aircraft still flying today — which aircraft?

Antonov An-124 Ruslan: Soviet military transport aircraft. Assembly of the first aircraft begun in 1979; the An-124 (which was sometimes referred to as the An-40 in the West) performed its maiden flight on 24 December 1982.
Most commonly caused by liver cirrhosis and its resulting high blood pressure in the portal system, this condition is the abnormal buildup of fluid in the abdominal cavity — which one?
Ascites: Abnormal build-up of fluid in the abdomen.
Instead of teeth, these marine mammals sieve plankton through whalebone plates in their mouths — a group of 16 species that includes the rorquals and the bowhead. What do we call them?
Both heads of this upper-arm muscle originate on the scapula and let you flex your elbow while turning your palm upward — what muscle is it?

Biceps: Muscle on the front of the upper arm. While the long head of the biceps crosses both the shoulder and elbow joints, its main function is at the elbow where it flexes and supinates the forearm.

Developed in the 1980s-90s to replace an aging Cold War transport aircraft, this large military cargo plane carries forward the name of two earlier piston-engined predecessors, the C-74 and C-124. What is this modern behemoth called?
Boeing C-17 Globemaster III: American four engine military transport aircraft.

Affecting roughly 22% of people worldwide, this oral parafunctional habit — often during sleep and without the person's awareness — can leave you with aching jaw muscles, headaches, and worn-down teeth. What is it?
Bruxism: Grinding or clenching of the teeth.
When this yeast infection strikes the mouth it's commonly called thrush, leaving telltale white patches on the tongue — what is the condition?
Candidiasis: Fungal infection due to any type of Candida.
Responsible for nearly 40 percent of blindness cases worldwide in 2020, this condition clouds the eye's lens and causes halos around lights — which condition?
Cataract: Clouding of the lens inside the eye, causing poor vision.
Known as lamb's quarters, goosefoot, or fat-hen, this fast-growing annual weed in the amaranth family is sometimes cultivated as food elsewhere — which plant?
Chenopodium album: Species of flowering plant in the goosefoot family.
Native to the Indonesian island that gave part of its scientific name, this legume flower also goes by butterfly pea or blue pea — what is it?

This small, ground-nesting game bird has a call of three quick chirps repeated in succession, breeds across Europe, and winters in Africa and southern India — which species, often confused with a similar-sounding Japanese cousin?
Common quail: Species of bird. The common quail (Coturnix coturnix) or European quail is a small ground-nesting game bird in the pheasant family Phasianidae.
This interdisciplinary field draws on sociology, psychology, and law to study crime, deviant behavior, and the workings of the justice system — what is it called?
Criminology: Field of studies related to crimes.
This Canadian-born entrepreneur co-founded and serves as CEO of Roblox Corporation, after his earlier company was acquired by MSC Software in 1998 — who is he?

Cultivated in China for more than 2,000 years despite not being formally described until 1780, this tree produces the most widely grown fruit in its genus, known by names like Japanese or Chinese persimmon. Which species?
Diospyros kaki: Oriental fruit. Although its first botanical description was not published until 1780, D. kaki cultivation in China dates back more than 2000 years.
Known medically as cerumen, this waxy secretion in the ear canal protects against bacteria, fungi, and water while trapping dust and dead skin — what is it?
Earwax: Waxy substance secreted by the ear.

Distinguished by its massive head, huge size, and trademark black facial mask, this gentle British dog breed is now classed as vulnerable in its homeland, with just 104 UK births recorded in 2020 — which breed?
English Mastiff: British breed of dog. The English Mastiff, or simply the Mastiff, is a British breed of very large dog of mastiff type.
This small European finch's male sports a blue-grey cap and rust-red underparts, while both sexes flash white wing bars — what species is it?
Eurasian chaffinch: Species of bird. The Eurasian chaffinch, common chaffinch, or simply the chaffinch (Fringilla coelebs) is a common and widespread small passerine bird – in the finch family.
A feathery, yellow-flowered Mediterranean herb in the carrot family, this anise-tasting plant is one of the primary ingredients in absinthe — what is it?
Fennel: Flowering plant species in the carrot family.
Named for the mathematician who used it to solve the heat equation, this expansion writes a periodic function as an infinite sum of sines and cosines — what is it?
Fourier series: Decomposition of periodic functions.
Commonly known as snails and slugs, this class is the second-largest in the animal kingdom after insects — what is it called?
Gastropod: Class of molluscs. The fossil record of gastropods extends back to the Late Cambrian.
Occurring in the cytosol, this ten-step metabolic pathway breaks glucose down into pyruvate while generating ATP and NADH — what process is it?
Glycolysis: Series of interconnected biochemical reactions.

Once nearly all lumped into a single genus before 21st-century research proved that grouping polyphyletic, these grey-and-white seabirds have an older dialect name, 'mew,' echoing their calls — which birds?
Gull: Subfamily of seabirds. The large species take up to four years to attain full adult plumage, but two years is typical for small gulls.
This medical term describes red blood cells rupturing and spilling their contents into the plasma — a process triggered by bacterial toxins or even intense exercise. What is it?
Hemolysis: Rupturing of red blood cells and release of their contents. Hemolysis may occur in vivo or in vitro.

The only birds whose first two neck vertebrae are fused together, these Old World birds have a long down-curved bill sometimes topped with a bony casque, and share an ecological niche with toucans in the Americas — which birds?
Hornbill: Family of birds. The family is omnivorous, feeding on fruit and small animals.

When the thyroid produces too little hormone, the body slows down — cold intolerance, fatigue, constipation, weight gain — and worldwide too little dietary iodine is the leading cause. What's the condition?
Hypothyroidism: Insufficient production of thyroid hormones.
Known naturally as the mineral hematite, this reddish compound with formula Fe2O3 is the main source for the steel industry and gets reduced by aluminum in the fiery thermite reaction — what is it?
Iron(III) oxide: Chemical compound. It occurs in nature as the mineral hematite, which serves as the primary source of iron for the steel industry.
Part of a four-person extremist cell known for English accents, this Kuwaiti-born militant appeared in Islamic State videos before being killed in a 2015 drone strike near Raqqa — who is he?
Jihadi John: Kuwaiti-British terrorist and ISIS executioner (1988–2015)
Named for a district in Turkey's Sivas Province, which large livestock guardian breed has been exported to Africa to protect flocks from cheetahs?
Kangal Shepherd Dog: Turkish breed of dog. The Kangal Shepherd Dog or Turkish Kangal (Turkish: Kangal Çoban Köpeği) is a traditional Turkish breed of large livestock guardian dog.
Native to North America and infamous for occasionally eating their mates after reproduction, the females of this venomous spider species sport striking black-and-red coloring — what species is it?
Latrodectus mactans: Species of spider. Latrodectus mactans, known as southern black widow or simply black widow, and the shoe-button spider, is a venomous species of spider in the genus Latrodectus.
This Australian speech and language therapist and amateur stage actor helped King George VI manage his stammer — who is he?
Lionel Logue: Australian speech and language therapist (1880–1953)
This flowering legume genus boasts over 199 species and has become such a successful invasive spreader in Iceland that it's now considered an ecological problem — which genus?
Dubbed "sea locusts" by the ancient Assyrians and "prawn killers" by others, these burrow-dwelling crustaceans are among the most important predators of shallow tropical seas. What are they?
Mantis shrimp: Order of crustaceans. Mantis shrimp are carnivorous marine crustaceans of the order Stomatopoda (from Ancient Greek στόμα (stóma) 'mouth' and πούς (poús) 'foot').

Fever, a fierce headache, neck stiffness, and a telltale rash that doesn't fade when a glass is rolled over it can signal this inflammation of the membranes around the brain and spinal cord — what is it?

Meningitis: Inflammation of membranes around the brain. Meningitis (pl. meningitides) is acute or chronic inflammation of the protective membranes covering the brain and spinal cord, collectively called the meninges.
Known to NATO as 'Flogger,' this Soviet variable-sweep-wing fighter was the first in the country's air force to carry look-down/shoot-down radar, with over 5,000 built. Which aircraft?
Mikoyan-Gurevich MiG-23: Soviet fighter-interceptor aircraft introduced in 1970.
Drawn from the latex of opium poppies, this naturally occurring opiate acts straight on the central nervous system to dull pain — but risks dependence and tolerance. What is it?
Morphine: Pain medication of the opiate family.
This chronic neurological disorder scrambles the sleep-wake cycle, bringing on excessive daytime sleepiness, sleep paralysis, and sudden episodes of muscle collapse called cataplexy — what is it?
Narcolepsy: Human sleep disorder. Narcolepsy is a chronic neurological disorder that impairs the ability to regulate sleep–wake cycles, and specifically impacts REM (rapid eye movement) sleep.
A catecholamine whose very name nods to the kidney, it acts as both a hormone and neurotransmitter and is called "noradrenaline" outside the US — what is it?
Norepinephrine: Catecholamine hormone and neurotransmitter. The general function of norepinephrine is to mobilize the brain and body for action.
Its Greek name means 'serpent-bearer,' and it's depicted as a man grasping a snake represented by a neighboring constellation — which constellation straddles the celestial equator?
Ophiuchus: Constellation straddling the celestial equator. Ophiuchus ( o-fee-YOO-kəs) is a large constellation straddling the celestial equator.
This butterfly was the first species to be given the common name now applied to its entire family, and is widespread across the Palearctic and North America — which species?
Papilio machaon: Species of insect. Papilio machaon, the Old World swallowtail, is a butterfly of the family Papilionidae.
In placental mammals, this is the region of the body between the anus and the genitals, running from the pubic bone to the tailbone, and is often considered an erogenous zone — what is it called?
Perineum: Region of the body between the genitals and anus. The perineum (pl.: perineums or perinea) in placental mammals is the space between the anus and the genitals.
This French physicist shared the 1903 Nobel Prize in Physics with his wife, making them the first married couple to win a Nobel — who is he?
Pierre Curie: French physicist and chemist (1859–1906)
Also called quaking aspen for the way its leaves flutter in the slightest breeze, which poplar species is native to the Old World's cool temperate regions?
Nicknamed 'gold cap' and 'golden halo,' this is the world's best-known psilocybin-containing mushroom thanks to its wide distribution and how easily it's cultivated — which species?
Psilocybe cubensis: Species of fungus. It belongs to the fungus family Hymenogastraceae and was previously known as Stropharia cubensis.
Also known as steelhead in its sea-run form, this North American Pacific species shows off a vivid reddish stripe along its flank in breeding males — which fish?
Rainbow trout: Fresh-water species of fish.
His 'Essai Sur La Nature Du Commerce' was called the 'cradle of political economy'; this Irish-French banker made a fortune speculating in John Law's Mississippi Company — who is it?
Richard Cantillon: Irish-French economist and banker (c. 1680 – 1734)
This extinct armored jawless fish from the Ordovician period had closely-spaced eyes at the front of its head, 'like car headlamps,' and is best known from fossils found in Bolivia — what is it?
Sacabambaspis: Extinct genus of jawless fishes.
Comprising seven species from the flatback to the leatherback, five of these ocean-dwelling reptiles are threatened with extinction — what are they?
Sea turtle: Reptiles of the superfamily Chelonioidea.
This small, wingless, primitive insect gets its common name from its grey sheen and darting, fish-like movements — and its scientific name hints at a diet of sugars and starches. What is it?
Silverfish: Small land insect in the order Zygentoma.
This healthcare discipline treats disorders of voice, fluency, and swallowing, practiced by clinicians licensed under boards overseen by groups like ASHA — which field of study?
Belonging to a fish family whose fossils date back to the Late Cretaceous, these long-lived, late-maturing fish share their order with paddlefish and once swam as far as North Africa — what are they?
Named after a figure from Greek mythology, this blue-gray transition metal with atomic number 73 is prized for corrosion resistance and shows up in capacitors inside computers. What element is this?
Tantalum: Chemical element with atomic number 73 (Ta)
This body region between the hip and the knee contains a single bone — the femur — that forms a ball-and-socket joint above and a hinge joint below. What is it?
Thigh: Body part between pelvis and knee; upper leg.
Also known as the windpipe, this cartilaginous tube linking the throat to the lungs is reinforced by horseshoe-shaped rings of cartilage — what is it?
Trachea: Cartilaginous tube. The trachea extends from the larynx and branches into the two primary bronchi.
Carrying the placeholder symbol Ubb, this hypothetical element 122 is expected to sit within the 'island of stability' — what is its systematic IUPAC name?
Unbibium: Theoretical chemical element with atomic number 122 (Ubb)
This chronic autoimmune disorder causes patches of skin to lose their pigment, and in antiquity it was so misunderstood that it was often confused with leprosy — what is it?
Vitiligo: Skin condition where patches lose pigment.
A short evergreen shrub with dull green leaves and orange-red berries, this nightshade-family plant is better known by names like Indian ginseng and winter cherry — what is it?
Withania somnifera: Species of flowering plant.
The symbol for silicon is Si. Silicon is a chemical element; it has symbol Si and atomic number 14.
The symbol for fermium is Fm. Fermium is a synthetic chemical element; it has symbol Fm and atomic number 100.

Tony Curtis: In his later years, Curtis made numerous television appearances.
In what year was Sarah Michelle Gellar born?
Sarah Michelle Gellar: Sarah Michelle Prinze (née Gellar GHEL-ər; born April 14, 1977) is an American actress.
In what year was Tilda Swinton born?
Tilda Swinton: Katherine Matilda "Tilda" Swinton (born 5 November 1960) is a Scottish actress.
In what year was Viola Davis born?
Viola Davis ( vy-OH-lə; born August 11, 1965) is an American actress and film producer.
In what year was Woody Allen born?
Woody Allen: Heywood "Woody" Allen (born Allan Stewart Konigsberg; November 30, 1935) is an American filmmaker, actor, writer, and comedian.
In what year was Alexander Skarsgård born?
Alexander Skarsgård: Alexander Johan Hjalmar Skarsgård (born 25 August 1976) is a Swedish actor.
In what year was Johnny Depp born?
